body.heading: The colleague nobody thanks
paragraphs: Every workplace runs on unglamorous kindness: the person who refills the shared printer, labels the leftovers, remembers how the new starter takes their tea. Noticing that work — and saying so once, specifically — costs nothing and is remembered for months.
Thank people in the channel they would prefer. Some love a public mention in the team meeting; others would rather have a quiet word or a note. Kindness that embarrasses is only half kind.

body.heading: Small helps that compound
paragraphs: Share the useful link instead of just the answer. Introduce the new person to one friendly face rather than the whole room. Offer your notes from the meeting someone missed before they have to ask. Each act is minutes long; together they build a reputation as the person who makes work lighter.

Covering for someone's difficult afternoon — the school call, the delivery, the appointment — is the heavyweight division of workplace kindness. It is repaid in trust, which is the currency everything else at work runs on.

body.heading: Kind is not the same as endlessly available
paragraphs: Boundaries keep kindness sustainable. You can be the colleague who helps gladly and still say, honestly, 'I can't today — try me Thursday.' Help that breeds resentment curdles; help with edges lasts a career.
And receive help as graciously as you give it. Workplaces become kind in both directions or neither; letting a colleague cover for you is part of the system, not a debt.

description: Noticing invisible work, sharing the useful link, covering a difficult afternoon: workplace kindness in minutes, not hours.
